title: Match Windows base images to a supported node OS
description: Validate the supported Windows host/container compatibility matrix. Windows Server 2019 node-pool support ended on 1 March 2026 and images are scheduled for removal on 1 April 2027. Migrate to a supported LTSC release such as Windows Server 2022 or 2025 after compatibility testing.

documentation.title: Match Windows base images to a supported node OS

title: Test graceful shutdown and recovery on Windows
description: Test SIGTERM-equivalent Windows shutdown behavior, preStop hooks, terminationGracePeriodSeconds, and actual application cleanup on supported Windows images. Avoid blanket claims that graceful termination is unavailable; design for abrupt failure and verify behavior during upgrades.

documentation.title: Test graceful shutdown and recovery on Windows

title: Restrict Windows HostProcess and administrative privileges
description: Run applications as a non-administrative identity where supported. Windows does not use Linux privileged-container semantics, but HostProcess containers can access the host and require tightly restricted admission, identities, and namespaces.

documentation.title: Restrict Windows HostProcess and administrative privileges

title: Set and monitor Windows memory requests and limits
description: Size Windows nodes and container memory using measured working sets and system reservations. Validate eviction and OOM behavior for the actual Windows/runtime version, alert on pressure, and test recovery rather than assuming Linux memory-management behavior.

documentation.title: Set and monitor Windows memory requests and limits

title: Choose a supported Azure CNI model for Windows
description: Use a Windows-supported Azure CNI configuration, including Overlay where supported for the selected versions. Kubenet and the Linux Cilium data plane are not Windows networking options. Validate policy-engine and IPAM support before provisioning.

documentation.title: Choose a supported Azure CNI model for Windows

title: Keep windows containers patch level in sync with host patch level
description: Windows Server nodes in AKS must be upgraded to get the latest patch fixes and updates. Windows Updates are not enabled on nodes in AKS. AKS releases new node pool images as soon as patches are available, it is the customers responsibility to upgrade node pools to stay current on patches and hotfix.

documentation.title: How do patch my Windows nodes?

title: Validate network policy enforcement on Windows
description: Do not assume Linux and Windows share the same network policy capabilities. Azure NPM on Windows is unsupported from 30 September 2026; select a supported alternative such as Calico after validating the exact OS, network model, and version matrix.

documentation.title: Validate network policy enforcement on Windows

title: Enable Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) for your Windows Server nodes
description: Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) is a managed domain account for multiple servers that provides automatic password management, simplified service principal name (SPN) management and the ability to delegate the management to other administrators.

documentation.title: Enable Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) for your Windows Server nodes

title: If required for AKS Windows workloads, HostProcess containers can be used
description: HostProcess / Privileged containers extend the Windows container model to enable a wider range of Kubernetes cluster management scenarios.

title: Taint Windows nodes
description: Adding taints, tolerations and node selectors will help avoid having pods scheduled in the wrong OS node pool

title: Migrate Windows Azure NPM policy before relying on enforcement
description: Inventory Windows pools using Azure Network Policy Manager, whose AKS Windows support ended on 30 September 2026. Follow supported migration guidance and test positive and negative connectivity cases with the replacement engine.

documentation.title: Migrate Windows Azure NPM policy before relying on enforcement

title: Validate accelerated networking for Windows node SKUs
description: Select a supported Windows VM size and verify accelerated networking availability and actual enablement. Benchmark throughput and latency, and include driver and node-image compatibility in upgrade testing.

title: Track Windows LTSC and Annual Channel retirement dates
description: Windows Server Annual Channel preview support ended on 15 May 2026, with image removal scheduled for 15 May 2027. Windows Server 2022 AKS support is scheduled to end on 30 June 2028, with image removal on 30 June 2029. Plan LTSC migration against current version and OS support matrices.

documentation.title: Track Windows LTSC and Annual Channel retirement dates
